title: Review of Singapore's Water Security Due to Rising Demands from Data Centres, Urban Expansion and Climate Variability
what_it_is: Review of Singapore's Water Security Due to Rising Demands from Data Centres, Urban Expansion and Climate Variability

sections.label: Water insecurity risks and Four National Taps
sections.summary: Singapore has diversified water supply through the Four National Taps, including weather-resilient desalinated water and NEWater, strengthening water security amid climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment with rising water demands from data centres, urban expansion and climate variability affecting local reservoirs (a) what is the latest assessment of Singapore's water insecurity risks, particularly ahead of the 2061 Johor Water Agreement expiry; and (b) what accelerated measures are being planned to ensure the Four National Taps meet future needs without compromising food production or household supply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We have diversified our water supply through the "Four National Taps".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These include desalinated water and NEWater, which are weather-resilient sources that strengthen our water security amid the effects of climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With the background that water scarcity has been intensified by climate change and the estimate is that there would be possible implications of up to 6% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2050, an impact on the GDP, and also, given that the World Bank has recently stated that the water will shift from a background resource to a binding constraint, then also, bearing in mind that if there is not good water management, there will also be constriction or a negative impact on the economic growth and given our expected increase in demands, including plans to build databanks and climate change driven increases, how is this systemic risk framing being incorporated into our fiscal and also forward estimates for public infrastructure demand planning parameters?

sections.label: Energy costs and desalinated water
sections.summary: Energy cost is a driver PUB focuses on, seeking technology to reduce water production costs, including energy, despite recent Middle East events.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that a lot of our water supply comes from very energy-intensive sources, like desalination, what is the impact that that increase in energy cost have had on the cost of our desalinated water?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And how are we responding to this prolonged energy price volatility, to moderate impact that the energy cost is having on our desalination cost modelling?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In Singapore, I would like to think that we have planned ahead, and we are always looking at the impact of climate change, as I have mentioned in my answer, and incorporating the impact of climate change in our long-term planning for our water infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: With regard to cost of energy, it is definitely a driver that we have always paid attention to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In fact, we set that as our goal so that our PUB colleagues will focus their attention on always searching for new technology that will reduce the overall costs of producing water, including energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And, of course, it has been exacerbated by recent events in Middle East, but that does not change our long-term focus on bringing down the costs of producing water, including the use of energy.
